name: IEEE 802.11 wireless local networking
description: A wireless local-area network standard specifying shared medium access and radio or other physical interfaces.

date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: IEEE published the original 802.11 wireless LAN standard.

evidence.supports: IEEE dates the standard and gives the 2 Mbit/s maximum.

events.caveats: The 2 Mbit/s figure is a technical maximum, not observed throughput, range, number of users or adoption.

events.statement: Apple introduced the iBook and AirPort as consumer wireless networking products.
events.caveats: The products used the later 802.11b generation; product introduction is not a count of buyers.

evidence.supports: IEEE identifies Apple’s products as 1999 examples.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced event establishing this scoped achievement; it is not a claim of global priority.

measures.subject: Original 1997 wireless LAN standard
measures.conditions: IEEE retrospective describes maximum; actual throughput varies and later amendments differ.

caveats: Earlier wireless local networks existed; 802.11 specifies a family of interoperable networking technologies, not all wireless networking.

research.note: New source-backed draft; independent review pending. Independent reader checked IEEE’s 1997 maximum and 1999 802.11b consumer example; figures are not observed throughput.
